PullRequest.Title: agentHost: Eagerly load set_workspace for workspaceless chats
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

- keep `set_workspace` deferred by default, but load it eagerly for workspaceless sessions
- separate workspaceless-session detection from provider workspace-conversion capability checks
- cover first-prompt workspace conversion through the real Copilot and Codex provider runtimes
- remove the resolved workspace-conversion known issue

## Testing

- `npm run compile` — passed
- `npm run hygiene` — passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionServerTools.test.ts --grep \"definitions and confirmation|set_workspace deferral follows|set_workspace is not advertised\"` — 3 passing
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep \"workspace conversion\"` — 1 passing
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/codexAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep \"workspace conversion\"` — 1 passing
- Azure pipeline definition 111 — not run yet; required cross-platform validation now that the PR exists

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or restore a workspaceless session and send the first or later Copilot prompt, including an optional workspace-conversion request.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session tool definitions are materialized synchronously before SDK tool registration and the existing provider model request. The diff marks exactly one tool, set_workspace, non-deferred for a workspaceless session; it adds no awaited operation or extra round trip. If the model calls it, the existing confirmation and workspace-conversion flow remains on the critical path by design.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the existing model request with set_workspace active instead of deferred for a workspaceless session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No additional network call; at most one bounded tool schema is added to each existing model step while the session remains workspaceless.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: On tool-search-enabled Copilot sessions, set_workspace was registered as deferred and omitted from the active tool set until loaded; Codex already ignored deferLoading and eagerly registered the same tool.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The metadata rides the existing provider request and may add a small fixed serialization/token cost, but adds no RTT or blocking operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register dynamic tools in the existing Codex thread/start request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing thread/start request per session materialization; tool count and payload are unchanged because Codex strips/ignores deferLoading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: set_workspace was already included eagerly in dynamicTools, and remains so.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No changed IPC work or payload on the Codex critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One set_workspace definition per workspaceless session. For a deferral-aware provider, its bounded description and two-property schema can be present on each model step while the session remains workspaceless; Codex already sends all dynamic tools eagerly, so its effective changed cardinality is zero.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider turn scheduling and concurrency are unchanged. There is still one provider request per model step for a chat, with no new fan-out, queue, or parallel boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The workspaceless check is an O(1) in-memory state/meta lookup. SDK tools are constructed at session materialization (and existing provider rebuild points); the change adds no cache, miss retry, or invalidation path. Whether the remote prompt cache reuses the stable tool prefix is provider-controlled, but the uncached addition is still only one bounded schema.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed deferLoading value and provider mappings are directly traced. High confidence that Copilot can eagerly expose one additional schema and Codex behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact tokenization and prompt-cache savings are provider/runtime dependent. The maximum changed metadata is nevertheless statically bounded to one small tool schema and no additional call, so this does not establish an actionable performance regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The small bounded eager-schema cost is the explicit mechanism required to make first-prompt workspace conversion available, and it adds neither boundary calls nor fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Advertise server tools when creating, restoring, or converting a session.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentServerToolHost.getDefinitionsForSession synchronously evaluates per-session metadata, then dispatches the same SessionServerToolsChanged action. The added work is one state lookup and, only for an eligible workspaceless session, one shallow definition copy.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch SessionServerToolsChanged to existing session clients.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing dispatch per create, restore, feature re-advertisement, or workspace conversion; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same action with the same protocol tool definitions was dispatched; deferLoading was already omitted from advertised state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The protocol conversion strips deferLoading, so the notification payload and boundary cost are unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and restore persisted session data before advertising tools.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing restore I/O per restored session; the new workspaceless predicate performs no filesystem access.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Restore performed the same persistence reads before the same advertisement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No filesystem call is added or moved by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Linear in sessions advertised during restore, with one additional O(1) lookup per advertisement rather than per tool, turn history item, or file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Advertisements retain their existing caller scheduling; no new Promise, task, queue, or concurrent operation is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The state manager is the authoritative in-memory source. No cache is bypassed or created, and conversion re-advertises after flipping the marker so subsequent definitions return to deferred.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the host implementation shows the added predicate is a direct map/property lookup and deferLoading is removed before protocol dispatch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session counts vary, but the added operation is a constant-time in-memory property check and at most one small object allocation per advertisement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added synchronous work is bounded and negligible, and existing IPC/I/O cardinality and payload are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Replay workspace-conversion E2E captures containing file://${workdir} placeholders.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each replay response already performs placeholder expansion before the local replay response is returned. The diff adds one URI conversion and one replaceAll scan in this test-only harness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Expand a file-URI workdir placeholder in serialized replay text.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional replaceAll pass per replayed response with a working directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The harness already made several full-text placeholder replacement passes but did not specially encode file URI placeholders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds a bounded test-harness string scan before returning the replay response; it is not on a shipped product path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing realpathSync attempt per replay response with a working directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same realpathSync attempt occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No new filesystem operation is introduced; the new replacement reuses the already resolved inputs.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One extra linear string scan per replay response that has a configured working directory; input size is the bounded capture response text, not product user data retained over time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Replay exchange concurrency and sequencing are unchanged; no additional request or worker is created.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. URI text is recomputed per replay response, matching the existing per-response placeholder substitutions; there is no long-lived retention.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line and enclosing harness method directly establish scope and multiplicity.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Capture response sizes vary, but this code is confined to integration tests and the added pass is one linear scan.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. This is a small test-only serialization cost with no product latency, throughput, or memory impact.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and every diff page. Traced eager tool loading through advertisement, Copilot/Claude/Codex provider mappings, session create/restore/conversion, and the replay harness. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
